title: Trump in China Special Coverage: Xi Warns Trump Over Taiwan, 'Issue Could Trigger Conflict'
description: Trump China Visit Live Updates: Follow real-time updates as US President Donald Trump arrives in Beijing for a high-stakes summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping, with global attention focused on whether Washington and Beijing can manage growing geopolitical and economic tensions. The two-day meeting is expected to address the Iran war, global trade, energy security, Taiwan, artificial intelligence and wider strategic competition between the United States and China.Trump’s First China Visit In Nine Years: President Donald Trump will arrive in Beijing on May 13, 2026, marking his first official visit to China since 2017 and his first trip to the country since returning to the White House for a second term. The summit comes at a particularly sensitive moment for global diplomacy and economic stability.Second Trump-Xi Meeting Since Return To White House: The Beijing summit will be only the second in-person meeting between Trump and Xi Jinping since Trump’s return to office, following their October 2025 talks in Busan, South Korea. Both leaders are expected to approach discussions cautiously amid strained bilateral ties.Iran War Expected To Dominate Discussions: The ongoing war involving Iran is expected to be one of the central issues on the agenda. Trump is likely to press Xi Jinping to use China’s influence with Tehran to help reopen the Strait of Hormuz and encourage renewed negotiations aimed at easing tensions in the Gulf.Trade And Economic Issues Back In Focus: Economic relations are expected to remain at the heart of the summit, with both sides discussing a possible extension of the existing trade truce. Talks may also include increased Chinese purchases of US goods, including Boeing aircraft, agricultural exports and energy products.Taiwan Remains Sensitive Flashpoint: Taiwan is expected to remain one of the most delicate issues during the summit. Beijing is likely to push for reduced US political and military support for the island, while Washington is expected to emphasise stability and deterrence in the Taiwan Strait.Artificial Intelligence And Technology Cooperation: The two countries may also discuss cooperation on artificial intelligence, particularly around risk management, regulation and the strategic implications of emerging technologies as competition intensifies between both powers.Additional Strategic Issues On Agenda: Other topics expected to surface include fentanyl trafficking, the case of Hong Kong activist Jimmy Lai, China’s nuclear weapons expansion and tensions in the South China Sea.Limited Expectations For Major Breakthroughs: Despite the high-profile nature of the meeting, analysts expect modest outcomes rather than sweeping agreements. The most likely results include limited economic deals, an extension of the current trade pause and commitments to continue high-level dialogue throughout 2026.Global Economic Pressure Shapes Summit: The summit takes place against the backdrop of the Iran conflict and a broader global energy crisis, which have driven oil prices higher and disrupted supply chains. Both Trump and Xi are facing economic pressure at home, with inflation and slowing growth affecting domestic political calculations.Critical Moment For Global Stability: The meeting is widely viewed as a major test of whether the United States and China can manage strategic rivalry without pushing the global economy and geopolitical order into deeper instability. With multiple crises unfolding simultaneously, the outcome of the summit is being closely watched around the world., World News News, Times Now

title: Iran crisis hampering aid to refugees as supply chain costs soar, UN warns
description: By Olivia Le PoidevinGENEVA, May 1 (Reuters) - The cost of sending some aid to Sudan - the world's largest displacement crisis - has more than doubled due to the Iran war, as shipping disruption pushes up costs and delays the delivery of relief, the U.N. refugee agency said on Friday.Heightened insecurity around key Gulf shipping routes, including the Strait of Hormuz, as well as congestion at ports, rising fuel prices and higher insurance premiums have all hampered the delivery of aid, particularly in Africa, the agency said.
